title: Experiment: keep the hidden manager page painted so Ctrl+1 skips the GPU repaint
notes:
From #314 (closed). Ctrl+1 to the manager takes about 88 ms median against 48 ms for a project tab. Most of the gap is the GPU redrawing the manager's text (~16 ms per arrival, ~30 ms in all), because hidden pages are moved off screen and lose their painted tiles. In one run, keeping the hidden manager painted brought Ctrl+1 to 56 ms, but alpha also moved to 56 ms. Hidden pages would also need `inert`, so they can't take focus or clicks.

Do: measure with measure.mjs manager-switch, 5+ runs each way, for both the manager and a project tab. Try keeping hidden pages painted (for example visibility or content-visibility rather than off-screen) with inert. Report the numbers. Ship it only if the manager switch gets faster and no tab gets slower; otherwise write the result in docs/performance/history.md and close. Do not bump the version.

comments.body: Rescope from main, 2026-11-26 check: scripts/performance/measure.mjs has no manager-switch mode any more (removed with #314); its keys step's tab-switch line (measure.mjs:183) already times Ctrl+1. Measure with that, record the result in docs/performance/history.md, and only change the app if the numbers show a gain.
